title: Expanded Report View
summary: open explicitly eligible Docs Viewer reports in a full-width view with temporary Manage-only column resizing
content_html:
Expanded Report View

Purpose

Allow an explicitly eligible Docs Viewer report to open from its ordinary report-host document in a full-width view. The expanded view preserves the live report and its current sorting, filtering, selection, actions, and report-owned route state rather than treating the report as a static table.

In Manage, an eligible tabular report can additionally expose temporary manual column-width controls. This brings the useful interaction from Markdown Table Detail to reports without applying the Markdown Table detail directive to code-generated content or assuming that every report uses the same semantic markup.

Current Starting Point

Reports owns the current report registry, metadata, implementations, and exact report-host model. Report Capability and Composition owns the shared, public, local-only, contribution, data, and stylesheet boundaries. Reports mount asynchronously into the generated host and choose semantic tables, lists, or sections from their own data relationship while remaining inside the normal document measure.

Report Blocks has shipped. One exact Report Block now supplies the validated descriptor and generated host; the retired document-level report front matter and append-after-content behavior are no longer supported.

Catalogue Works Report Migration has also shipped. Its search-driven local catalogue_works report is the motivating wide tabular report and already supplies semantic HTML table structure, stable columns, sorting, and an explicit clipboard projection. Expanded Report View remains the sole owner of rehosting, horizontal scrolling, and temporary manual widths.

Docs Viewer Panel Hosts and Control Surfaces owns the existing public/Manage Content Detail view and its expanded-main layout. Markdown Table Detail registers one exact marked semantic table, clones it into that view, and adds Manage-only resize and copy tools through the presentation lifecycle.

Reports cannot safely reuse the table clone. They are live components whose event listeners and internal state belong to the mounted report, and some reports rebuild their header and rows after sorting or filtering. The expanded report must therefore rehost the exact live report root and restore it on Back.

Current report layouts are designed to fit or reflow within the document measure. They have no general report-owned horizontal scroll viewport, so a future report with meaningful minimum column widths needs an explicit expanded presentation rather than accidental page overflow.

ERV-1 — Expanded Report View Delivery is the active bounded implementation and evidence plan. ERV-1.1 has shipped the public-safe live-report expansion foundation; the current public entrypoint also composes it, but no public or local report opts in yet. ERV-1.1R is now the pending corrective checkpoint that removes this unused public composition before ERV-1.2 Catalogue Works adoption and Manage-only widths.

Safety, Composition, And Adoption

Report Capability and Composition distinguishes three states that file paths do not reveal:

  • Public-safe: the adapter and its dependencies are permitted to execute over public data and carry no local or management authority. A file under site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/ can have this property without being downloaded by a public route.
  • Publicly composed: the public entrypoint imports and wires the adapter, or the public shell loads CSS containing its selectors. This causes the code or CSS bytes to be downloaded even when no report invokes them.
  • Publicly adopted: an explicitly promoted public report returns the capability handle and uses the composed adapter. Adoption still requires its own public data, metadata, executable loader, and report contract.

The equivalent local states are independent. Manage can compose and adopt one public-safe implementation without the public entrypoint composing it and without creating a public report.

At the ERV-1.1 review gate, site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js is public-safe and is statically imported and constructed by site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/public/docs-viewer-public.js. Its control and viewport selectors are also present in the public-loaded site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-reports.css. Expanded Report View is therefore publicly composed today. The public loader still exposes only docs_subscope, that module does not return expandedPresentation, and no other report returns it yet. The public composition is consequently unused; its presence is not evidence that a public report needs expansion or that one will exist.

Public safety alone does not authorize public composition. The default boundary is to compose Expanded Report View only in a shell with a named current adopter. catalogue_works can become the first Manage adopter without public composition. If a future public report needs expansion, its delivery can add the public import and stylesheet edges alongside the report's explicit public promotion. Keeping the implementation public-safe makes that later reuse possible; it does not require speculative public download now.

Report Presentation Boundary

New reports choose their semantic structure from the report requirement rather than inheriting one universal visual implementation.

  • A stable rectangular dataset whose rows share named columns should normally use a semantic HTML table with thead, tbody, column headers, rows, and cells. Sorting links, selection controls, and other interactive content can remain inside that structure.
  • A navigable collection, heterogeneous list, grouped summary, card-like result, or composition whose rows do not share one stable column relationship should use the corresponding list or section semantics and may use CSS Grid for layout.
  • CSS remains responsible for presentation in either case. The distinction is semantic HTML table versus list/section markup laid out with Grid, not CSS versus HTML.

An existing report may change representation when its requirement evolves. In practice, the likely direction is list/Grid to semantic table when a report acquires durable columns, header relationships, resizing, or tabular export. Table to list/Grid remains possible when a report stops being meaningfully rectangular, but that is a broader requirements change and may be clearer as a new report presentation rather than a silent rewrite. Representation is not report identity: a conversion retains the report id, exact data authority, access boundary, and route-state contract unless a separate feature changes them.

Proposed Feature Contract

  • Eligibility is declared explicitly by a report or report preset. Width, row count, headings, DOM shape, or measured overflow never grants eligibility.
  • The report or preset declares the presentation kind required by its data relationships. Expanded Report View does not impose Grid or semantic table markup on every report.
  • The open control becomes available only after the exact report has mounted successfully. Its target retains the current scope, parent doc_id, report id, preset or collection context where applicable, and document-mount generation. A document hosts at most one report, so the target has no report-instance identity or instance-prefixed state.
  • Opening the report uses the existing public/Manage Content Detail view and expanded-main layout. The sidebar and Info panel are projected away temporarily while their state is retained.
  • The presentation rehosts the live report root; it does not clone the report, mount a second copy, refetch its data, or create a parallel report state owner.
  • Back restores the live report to its original document position, scroll position, and invocation focus. Document navigation releases the expanded target without restoring stale context.
  • The ordinary embedded report keeps its current fit-and-reflow presentation. Expanded Report View does not make horizontal scrolling the default for normal report documents.
  • The expansion adapter remains public-safe, but each shell composes it only for a named current adopter. Manage adoption does not imply public composition; a future public adopter requires an explicit public import and stylesheet decision.
  • When public composition exists, public runtime must not import Manage-only resizing tools or gain write-capable handles.
  • Manage-only manual resizing requires an explicit tabular column model with stable column ids, labels, and ordered header/row correspondence. Non-tabular reports remain expandable without resize handles.
  • Resize handles support pointer dragging and keyboard Left/Right adjustment. Widths are applied through the presentation's single column owner: a colgroup for a semantic table or one root-owned track template for an explicitly tabular Grid presentation. Every current or subsequently rendered row retains the same widths.
  • Increasing the total column width beyond the available expanded view produces bounded horizontal scrolling inside the expanded report viewport.
  • Reset widths removes the temporary override and restores the report or preset's natural responsive table or Grid layout.
  • Manual widths are presentation-session state only. They are not written to source front matter, report registry data, URLs, browser storage, canonical data, or generated payloads, and they are discarded when the expanded view closes.

Boundaries

This feature does not:

  • apply the Markdown Table detail directive or data-docs-content-detail="table" marker to reports;
  • require a wholesale conversion of existing reports to one markup model or retain parallel Grid/table renderers for compatibility;
  • infer report identity, eligibility, or columns from labels, rendered child counts, geometry, overflow, the selected row, or the current route alone;
  • add column resizing to the normal embedded report presentation;
  • persist personal layouts or introduce saved report views;
  • add a generic dashboard, arbitrary report plugin registry, report designer, or user-defined columns;
  • give public routes management controls, local services, source access, or write authority;
  • treat the existing Markdown Copy table action as automatic report functionality, because a report's interactive DOM is not itself a semantic export contract;
  • require every current report to opt in, including non-tabular reports and sub-scope child-detail states; or
  • broaden local Docs Viewer into a phone-specific layout. Public report presentation retains its existing mobile responsibility.

Discussion Position

The preferred ownership shape is one exact public-safe report-presentation adapter plus a Manage-only column-width extension, following Report Capability and Composition. The report supplies its semantic presentation kind and, when tabular, its stable column model; the adapter owns expanded presentation and lifecycle; the Manage extension owns representation-aware resize interaction, Reset widths, and its local stylesheet; each report remains the sole owner of its data, rows, filters, sorting, selection, actions, and route state. Manage may compose this public-safe adapter without public composition. A public entrypoint imports it only for a named public adopter and never imports the width controller or loads its stylesheet.

The Report Blocks and Catalogue Works prerequisites are now shipped. ERV-1 proposes the shared contract and adopts catalogue_works, which already supplies semantic table structure, stable columns, search, sorting, exact links, and Copy table. project_state remains a possible later adoption rather than a prerequisite conversion. docs_subscope customisations should be assessed separately because their visual columns can be composed from collection-specific contributions and selection state.

ERV-1 resolves the declaration as an optional expandedPresentation handle returned by a successful report-module mount. The handle owns the presentation kind and, for a semantic table, its stable column model and rerender subscription. It does not duplicate the report registry or project management configuration to public routes.

Potential Delivery Shape

  1. Expanded Report foundation — add exact report registration, live-root rehosting, Back/navigation lifecycle, the bounded expanded viewport, and explicit shell composition without column resizing. ERV-1.1 implemented public and Manage composition; the public edge is currently unused and must be reconciled with the named-adopter rule before completion.
  2. Public-composition correction — retain the public-safe shared implementation and Manage composition while removing the adapter, registration, and selectors from the public graph until a named public adopter exists.
  3. Managed report widths — add the explicit column model, accessible resize handles, representation-owned width projection, bounded horizontal scrolling, Reset widths, and catalogue_works adoption.
  4. Additional report adoption — opt in other tabular reports only after their stable column ownership is explicit; treat composite sub-scope customisations as a separate independently useful result if they require a broader contract.

ERV-1 maps the foundation, public-composition correction, and managed-width outcomes into explicit review-gated checkpoints and leaves additional report adoption deferred. ERV-1.1 is complete; ERV-1.1R is specified and parked before implementation approval. The foundation exists, no report has adopted it, and the unused public composition is now an explicit correction rather than an implication of the shared file path.

ERV-1.1R Acceptance Reminder

Carry these points through implementation, ERV-1 closeout, and the durable Reports and Report Capability and Composition owners:

  • site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-report-presentation.js remains public-safe, publicly addressable, and listed in the site runtime manifest; none of those facts means a public browser downloads it.
  • The public entrypoint and its transitive import graph do not import or construct the adapter until a named public report adopts it.
  • The public document-extras and report-controller path does not receive or register expandedPresentation; those explicit edges belong to a future public adoption.
  • The public-loaded site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer-reports.css contains no expansion control or viewport selectors. Manage receives those selectors from its local report stylesheet.
  • Manage imports, constructs, supplies, and releases the exact public-safe adapter through the retained shared Content Detail and lifecycle injection seams.
  • No report adoption, column model, resize handle, width state, data request, registry, payload, service, or route change is part of ERV-1.1R, so visible product behavior remains unchanged.
  • A future public adoption must add the public entrypoint, controller, and stylesheet edges explicitly alongside a named report's public data, metadata, loader, and behavior contract.
  • ERV-1.3 must transfer the shipped safety/composition/adoption boundary into Reports and Report Capability and Composition; the delivery record alone is not the durable authority.

Docs Viewer Capability Composition Audit separately proposes the checked manifest and automatic audit that will make these declarations printable across capabilities. ERV-1.1R remains responsible for correcting the Expanded Report implementation now; it does not wait for or implement that general audit feature.

Success Meaning

The feature succeeds when an eligible report can open in the full-width Content Detail layout without losing or duplicating its live state, return safely to the ordinary document, and remain exact across navigation. In Manage, an eligible declared column model can be resized accessibly, remain aligned through report rerendering, scroll within the expanded viewport when widened, and return to its natural responsive template through Reset widths. Public routes carry no expansion code or selectors merely because the implementation is public-safe; they compose the read-only presentation only when a named public report adopts it, and they never receive management capability.
